'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Iranian involvement in the Syrian civil war]]
***A [[Drone warfare|drone strike]] on a [[Iran]]ian-backed [[weapons factory]] by an unknown attacker in [[Deir ez-Zor Governorate]], [[Syria]], kills seven people and injures 15 others, according to the [[Syrian Observatory for Human Rights]], which describes the dead as three [[Afghans|Afghan]] fighters, three [[Syrians|Syrian]] [[civilian]]s and one unidentified Syrian. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2264596/middle-east (Arab News)]
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**Thirty-five people are killed after [[Islamism|Islamist]] militants attack the village of Mukondi, [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/least-36-killed-east-congo-village-attack-local-official-civil-society-survivor-2023-03-09/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[Governor of California|California Governor]] [[Gavin Newsom]] tests positive for [[COVID-19]] for a second time. [https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/california/governor-newsom-covid-positive/3175198/ (KNTV)]
 
'''Law and crime'''
*[[List of foreign nationals detained in Iran|Foreign nationals detained in Iran]]
**A court in [[Iran]] [[sentence (law)|sentences]] a 64-year-old [[Republic of Ireland|Irish]]-[[French people|French]] [[tourism in Iran|tourist]] to six-and-a-half years in prison for [[Espionage|spying]] for "an enemy country". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-64888224 (BBC News)]
*[[Killing of Breonna Taylor]]
**The [[United States Department of Justice]] finds "reasonable cause to believe" that the [[Louisville Metro Police Department]] violated citizens' [[civil rights]]. The investigation was started after the fatal shooting of Breonna Taylor. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-64892223 (BBC News)]
